one_month_reasoning: The window's last close is Fri 2026-10-30, because 11/01 is a Sunday. No Q3 date has been announced. EDGAR shows past Q3 prints on Nov 2-7 (source 27), and calendar sites estimate Nov 3-5 (source 8), so the Q3 print falls outside the window with ~95% probability. The residual risk is a pre-announcement tied to a capital-markets action, as on July 7, 2026. Q3 guidance ($304-307M, +32-34%; source 1) makes a negative pre-announcement unlikely. In-window inputs are mildly positive but weak: the Silicon Data neo-cloud H100 rental index is $2.78/hr, +3% w/w (source 24), and CME H100/B200 compute futures list on Oct 5 (source 25), which keeps attention on GPU-capacity owners; Finviz also notes a recent Stifel upgrade to Buy (source 21). These are offset by a pre-earnings positioning run-up risk going both ways, ongoing small 10b5-1 sales (source 3) and neocloud-sentiment contagion. With no scheduled catalyst, I keep a near-symmetric lognormal around spot (median ~$140.5) at monthly sigma ~22% (82%/3.5 = 23%). P(>=140.07) = 0.50.

fair_value.method: Horizon (Oct-2027) value on NTM ~ CY2028 numbers, using 125M diluted shares and ~$1.0B horizon net debt (finance leases incl. MUFG draws, excl. operating leases). EV/Sales 6.5x (12-peer CY27 median) on $2.45B = $119; EV/EBITDA 16x (peer median ~15.6x) on $0.93B = $111; P/E 36x (PEG-parity vs the 23.7x infrastructure median, inside the 14.5-209x range) on $2.40 = $86. Weighted 0.35/0.35/0.30 = ~$107.

bear.story: AI-infrastructure de-rating combined with an execution wobble. Nine-figure commitments ramp late, gross margin keeps sliding as GPU depreciation rises, and the lease-funded build (MUFG draws, $2.76B uncommenced operating leases) pushes FCF to ~zero. The 2027 growth guide comes in at 35-40% rather than 50%+. The stock trades at the infrastructure median (~24x CY28 EPS, ~4.5-5x sales).

base.story: DOCN delivers ~50% 2027 growth and guides 2028 to ~35%, with adj. EBITDA in the high-30s. The multiple compresses from ~78x to ~55x NTM EPS and from ~10x to ~7.5x sales as growth normalises, so earnings growth roughly offsets the de-rating. The stock ends a little below today's price but above my ~$107 peer-bounded fair value, because a residual AI-growth premium persists while GPU rental pricing stays firm.

bull.story: Inference demand compounds: the H100/B200 rental indices keep rising, more nine-figure contracts land, RPO passes $2B and 2028 is guided toward the +48% thin consensus. The market pays 10-12x forward sales, and the stock retakes and exceeds the $187.50 high.

comps_summary.peer_range: All P/E figures are on one basis: calendar-2027 street (non-GAAP) EPS from Finviz at 2026-10-02 prices. MSFT and ORCL are calendarized, and January fiscal years (MDB, SNOW) are treated as CY27. stockanalysis 'Forward PE' is not used. P/E: 14.5x-208.7x across 10 profitable peers, median 32.3x. The infrastructure subset (AKAM, NET, FSLY, AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, ORCL) has a median of 23.7x; the developer-software subset (DDOG, MDB, SNOW) is 45-113x. CRWV and NBIS are NM on P/E (losses). Forward EV/EBITDA, CY27: 7.5x-29.5x across the 7 peers with meaningful EBITDA, median 15.6x. CRWV is MarketScreener consensus; the others are EV / TTM EBITDA scaled to CY27 revenue at constant margin. It is NM for NET, FSLY, DDOG, MDB and SNOW (TTM GAAP EBITDA ~0, Finviz 575-1184x). EV/Sales CY27: 3.0x-33.4x, median 6.5x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: Today DOCN trades at ~78x CY27 EPS ($140/$1.80), ~24x CY27 EV/EBITDA (EV ~$17.8B / ~$0.73B) and ~9.8x CY27 EV/Sales. That is above the peer median on every measure but inside each range. My fair value uses 36x P/E (11% above the 32.3x full median, ~52% above the 23.7x infrastructure median), 16x EV/EBITDA (at the 15.6x median) and 6.5x EV/Sales (at the median), all applied to CY2028E (horizon NTM).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: There is no premium on EV/Sales or EV/EBITDA; both sit at the peer median. The P/E premium over the infrastructure median is a growth adjustment, not a re-rating call. Infrastructure peers trade at ~1.2x PEG on ~20% median EPS growth. DOCN's ~33% EPS growth through the horizon is largely contracted: $894M RPO with >3-yr life ($366M within 12 months), nine-figure multi-year AI commitments, and ~155MW of committed capacity. That gives ~39x at PEG parity, and I take 3 turns off because the economics are weaker than the peers': gross margin is falling (59.9% to 55.0%) and growth is funded with leases and equity, so it converts to EPS less fully. The resulting 36x is inside the peer range and near the full-set median. Sell-side outperform calls are not used.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$80, DOCN trades at ~44x CY27 EPS, ~5.7x CY27 EV/Sales ((80 x 125M + $0.28B)/$1.81B) and ~14x CY27 EBITDA. That is the infrastructure-peer median with no growth premium, and 25% below my $107 fair value. Holding there would most likely mean the contracted growth is breaking: nine-figure AI commitments delayed or cancelled, RPO shrinking, the 2027 guide well below 50%, or GPU rental prices rolling over (Silicon Data H100 index turning down). Ordinary 80%-vol noise can visit $80, but a sustained level there would be fundamental.

These help per-share value, but for a horizon valuation the relevant figure is net debt after a year of MUFG finance-lease draws, ~$1.0B, which is above my round-1 $0.8B, so the net effect is small. On comps, I rebuilt on one Finviz CY27 street-EPS basis with 12 peers, adding the hyperscalers (AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT) and dropping IREN and GTLB. The P/E median is 32.3x overall and 23.7x for infrastructure. I replaced my 47x (a software-heavy median) with 36x, justified by PEG rather than by a premium. EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA now sit at the peer medians (6.5x, 16x). I raised CY28 revenue to $2.45B, informed by the thin +48% MarketScreener consensus. Fair value falls from $118 to ~$107. In lane, as the supervisor advised, I now weight GPU rental pricing above web-traffic and forum signals. Silicon Data's neo-cloud H100 index is $2.78/hr, +3% w/w (source 24). SemiAnalysis, via NextBigFuture, describes a renewed spot 'hard squeeze' (source 26), and CME launches compute futures on Oct 5 (source 25). This supports pricing on DOCN's new capacity and lifts the bull tail somewhat. I demote the Similarweb -8% m/m, the HN Hetzner thread and the OpenRouter rank to minor colour: one month of noisy data, and OpenRouter misses direct inference contracts. Distribution: a lognormal mixture of bear $72/25%, base $135/50% and bull $230/25% gives a mean of ~$143 and a median just below spot. P(>=140) = 0.465, down from 0.49, because fair value is lower and the stock trades at ~78x CY27 EPS against a 23.7-32x peer anchor. That is partly offset by contracted growth momentum and firm GPU pricing. With 82% realised vol, both tails stay fat. Research was limited to ~4 searches plus targeted fetches.
